gaps.what: Who held the Pingliang (Zhangyi), Guyuan and southern Ningxia country in 916-924: still recorded as nobody at confidence 1. The Zhu Wen page is silent on Pingliang, Zhangyi, Guyuan and Jingyuan; the Li Maozhen page has only Liu Zhijun made governor of Zhangyi in winter 908 and fleeing to Shu after 915.

Zhu Wen's 907-912 territory and the 911-914 outline stay Cliopatria's (minus Jingnan, plus Yan'an from 908): the Zhu Wen page lists no territory. The Wei Prefecture (Puyang) attack is dated only to the Zhao campaign (921 to late 922); Shandong north of the river is kept for lack of a page.

Cession year of the Sixteen Prefectures stays disputed (promised 936 in the Five Dynasties and Taizong of Liao pages; ceded 938 three times and 937 once on the Sixteen Prefectures page); the Liao dossier (ea-05) must agree with the 938 loss. Fan Yanguang's revolt has no month on its page (summer 937 march, fall 938 surrender).

counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Fan Yanguang's revolt (Tianxiong, Yedu): rebel state that held the Tianxiong circuit from 937 to fall 938

problems: Fix round applied to qi-kingdom, later-liang-dynasty and later-jin only; former-shu, min, southern-chu and yin-ten-kingdoms were not touched. All three validate with --resolve: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Mirror events wanted in dossiers other batches own: former-jin (gains from later-liang-dynasty: Tianxiong 915, the north bank including Henan north of the river 916, Zhao 922; a loss of Wei Prefecture (Puyang) in 921-922; a loss of the Zhaoyi circuit (Li Jitao) in spring 923); liao-dynasty (ea-05: vassal pair for later-jin, 936/11 to 942, suzerain as counterpart; the Sixteen Prefectures); later-tang (the events of 19 November 923, spring 923 and 11 January 937 listed in the notes).

later-liang-dynasty: the first notes gave the corrected 916 outline as about 733,900 km2; by cell count it is 68 percent of Cliopatria's 793,636 km2 (about 543,000 km2). Corrected in the dossier's notes.

later-liang-dynasty: one addition beyond the reviewer's list. The Tianxiong 80 km disc is cut in the 915, 916-921 and 922 keyframes so that the 915 loss and the keyframes agree for its Shandong and Henan cells.
qi-kingdom: Fengxiang's 30 km disc is added to the keyframe unions; the Baoji 40 km disc did not contain it, which had left three cells appearing in 916 with no event.

later-jin: a contest_start/contest_end pair names the free string 'Fan Yanguang's revolt (Tianxiong)' as counterpart; if a rebel dossier is written, the counterpart should become its slug and the Tianxiong land a loss in 937 and a gain in 938.
Radii of the Jingnan (40 km each at Bin, Ning, Qing) and Yan'an (80 km) discs are the author's readings; the reviewer's examples used 15 km. The pages give no boundary for any circuit.

Disagreement with the review notes (remark only, not a finding): they say the historical seat of 衛州 was near Weihui (Xinxiang); no page opened says so, so the drawing follows the Zhu Youzhen page (Puyang).
WebFetch returns model summaries of the pages, not page text; quotes in the fix-round notes are the sentences the summaries returned.
